compactMembership.notes: Both Utah's Oregon-reciprocity and general-endorsement mechanisms result in Utah issuing its own distinct Master Electrician certificate — not a single multistate license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact, e.g. the Nurse Licensure Compact). Recorded as false, matching the same reasoning already applied to every other electrician state file.

reciprocityRules.value: Utah has exactly one formal, no-examination bilateral reciprocal agreement for master-level electricians: with Oregon (Agreement BCD# 73-0-452). Under it, Utah issues a Master Electrician certificate WITHOUT EXAMINATION to a holder of an Oregon General Supervising Electrician license (and Oregon reciprocates for Utah Master Electrician certificate holders, issuing a General Supervising Electrician license), provided: the original license/certificate was obtained BY EXAMINATION with a minimum score of 75%; it is current, active, and in good standing; and the holder worked as a licensed journeyman electrician for at least 4 years (8,000 hours) — or equivalent experience as determined by the licensing state. No other state-specific no-exam reciprocal agreement was found for Utah master licensure; for every other state, applicants use Utah's broader ENDORSEMENT pathway instead, which does NOT waive Utah's own exam (see endorsementRules and requiredExams).

reciprocityRules.notes: A commonly repeated secondary-source claim (multiple contractor-license aggregator blogs — servicetitan.com, contractorlicenserequirements.com, ultimateelectriciansguide.com, sparkshift.app, and others) states Utah has bilateral reciprocity with Arizona, Nevada, Idaho, Colorado, and Wyoming. This was actively investigated: the official DOPL 'equivalent states' endorsement-map PDFs referenced by the Journeyman and Master out-of-state-by-endorsement pages (endorsement-to-utah-journeyman-electrician.pdf, endorsement-to-utah-master-electrician.pdf) returned HTTP 403 on every automated fetch attempt (multiple tries, including a retry after the user manually accessed the surrounding HTML pages), and no official source confirming or denying this specific 5-state list was found anywhere. It is NOT included as fact here — absence of confirmation is treated as absence, not silently assumed true. This gap should be revisited if the endorsement-map PDFs become reachable.

endorsementRules.value: For any state OTHER than Oregon, an out-of-state master electrician license holder must apply through Utah's general licensure-BY-ENDORSEMENT pathway (Utah Code 58-1-302; Utah Admin. Code R156-1-302). Unlike Oregon reciprocity, this pathway does NOT waive Utah's own examination: DOPL's own Master Electrician Out-of-State Applicants Applying by Endorsement page states explicitly, 'All applicants will be required to pass the Utah Master Electrician Law and Rule examination,' regardless of the applicant's origin state or existing license.

endorsementRules.notes: Utah is the first of PermitBridge's electrician states where 'reciprocity' and 'endorsement' are genuinely distinct, separately governed pathways rather than interchangeable terminology — every prior state (Colorado, Virginia, Texas, Arkansas, Minnesota) left this field Unknown because no such distinction existed in their materials.

requiredExams.value: Via the Oregon RECIPROCITY pathway: no additional Utah examination — the agreement issues the certificate 'without examination' provided the original exam score was at least 75%. Via the general ENDORSEMENT pathway (all other states): DOPL's own Master Electrician Out-of-State Applicants Applying by Endorsement page states explicitly, 'All applicants will be required to pass the Utah Master Electrician Law and Rule examination' — a real, confirmed exam requirement, not merely discretionary language. This is a genuine, directly-quoted distinction from Oregon's true no-exam reciprocity.

requiredExperience.notes: For ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) Utah master licensure, a secondary-source synthesis (not independently confirmed against DOPL's own text) describes 8,000 hours of journeyman experience (4,000 hours with a 2-year AAS electrical trade degree; 2,000 hours with a B.S. in electrical engineering from an ABET-accredited program), plus passing Utah's Electrical Licensing Theory, Code, and Practical Examinations. Not recorded as the field's value since it wasn't independently verified against a primary source; noted here only for context.

requiredEducation.notes: No standalone formal-education requirement distinct from the experience pathways already captured in requiredExperience was confirmed from a primary source — matching the same scope decision already made across every other electrician state file.

requiredDocuments.notes: The Oregon agreement references each state maintaining and exchanging qualification records, but does not itemize a specific applicant-facing document checklist. DOPL's own application-document pages returned HTTP 403 on most automated fetch attempts.

continuingEducationRequirements.notes: Secondary sources (continuing-education course vendors, not DOPL itself) describe a 16-hour/2-year cycle (12 core + 4 flexible, renewing Nov 30 of even years) applying to both Journeyman and Master, but none of this was confirmed against DOPL's own rule text or renewal page — both were unreachable throughout this research. Left Unknown rather than sourced to commercial CE-vendor content, which does not meet this project's authoritative-source bar.
